_about: Public-domain Newell Dwight Hillis (1858-1929), Beecher's successor at Plymouth Church, Brooklyn, for the Word Hoard: his religious books, A Man's Value to Society (fifth edition, 1897), The Investment of Influence (1898), Foretokens of Immortality (copyright 1897), How the Inner Light Failed (1897-98), The Influence of Christ in Modern Life (1900), The Quest of Happiness (1902) and The Great Refusal (1923), from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-18 by lane A, round 36 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

ndhillis-mans-value: A Man's Value to Society: Studies in Self-Culture and Character, fifth edition (New York, Chicago, Toronto: Fleming H. Revell, 1897)
ndhillis-investment-influence: The Investment of Influence: A Study of Social Sympathy and Service (New York, Chicago, Toronto: Fleming H. Revell, 1898)
ndhillis-foretokens: Foretokens of Immortality (New York, Chicago, Toronto: Fleming H. Revell; title page undated, copyright 1897)
ndhillis-inner-light: How the Inner Light Failed, with How the Inner Light Grows (New York, Chicago, Toronto: Fleming H. Revell; copyright 1897 and 1898)
ndhillis-influence-christ: The Influence of Christ in Modern Life (New York and London: Macmillan, 1900)
ndhillis-quest-happiness: The Quest of Happiness: A Study of Victory over Life's Troubles (New York and London: Macmillan, 1902)
ndhillis-great-refusal: The Great Refusal and Other Evangelistic Sermons (New York, Chicago, Toronto: Fleming H. Revell; copyright 1923)

_alternates.ndhillis-copies: Later editions of Man's Value and Investment (PG 28875, PG 17274); Right Living as a Fine Art (PG 36695, 1903); The Quest of John Chapman, a novel (1904)

_excluded.ndhillis-other: His war books (PG 18557, 49515, 22821); Beecher's and Swing's books, which he edited
